question: Compare memory bandwidth of the Apple M4 Pro and M5 Pro.
raw_answer: The memory bandwidth of the Apple M5 Pro is 307 GB/s [1], while the memory bandwidth of the Apple M4 Pro is 273 GB/s [4]. Therefore, the M5 Pro has higher memory bandwidth than the M4 Pro.

passages.heading: Super cores and performance cores
passages.text:
Both M5 Pro and M5 Max use the identical CPU split: 18 cores made up of 6 “super cores” and 12 performance cores. Apple uses “super core” as a label across its 2026 chip family, including M6, but has not published a technical definition distinguishing a super core from a performance core beyond the naming itself.

Where the two chips diverge is the GPU and memory ceiling. M5 Max’s GPU scales to 40 cores against M5 Pro’s 20, and its memory ceiling doubles, from 64GB to 128GB, with bandwidth nearly doubling too, from 307GB/s to 614GB/s. Both chips share a 16-core Neural Engine.

passages.heading: Performance claims, and what Apple compares them to
passages.text:
Apple publishes no independent benchmark for either chip. Every number below is Apple’s own claim against the comparison point Apple names.

| Claim | Apple’s stated comparison |
|---|---|
| CPU multithreaded: up to 30% boost (M5 Pro) | vs. M4 Pro |
| CPU multithreaded: up to 15% boost (M5 Max) | vs. M4 Max |
| GPU AI compute: over 4x peak | vs. previous generation |
| Ray-traced graphics: up to 35% uplift | vs. M4 Pro/Max |
| General graphics: up to 20% higher | vs. M4 Pro/Max |

            Benchmarks & Specs

The Apple M5 Pro in the version with 18 CPU cores and 20 GPU cores is the larger of the two Pro variants of the M5 generation and launched in the MacBook Pro in the first quarter of 2026. It is aimed at professional users in software development, photo and video editing, 3D and music production who need more performance than the standard M5 offers. The chip is manufactured by TSMC in a 3 nm process.

sources.title: Apple M4 vs Apple M4 Pro (14-CPU 20-GPU) - Benchmark, comparison and differences
sources.site_name: Apple M4 vs Apple M4 Pro (14-CPU 20-GPU)

passages.text:
Last updated: 

        VS

            The Apple M4 is designed for efficiency and balanced performance in general use. The **Apple M4** Pro (14-CPU 20-GPU) is aimed at professional users who require peak performance for demanding workloads.

Both processors are manufactured by Apple using the 3 nm process and utilize the M4 architecture. The Apple M4 features a 10-core CPU, an Apple M4 (10 Core) GPU, and 20 MB of L2 cache. The Apple M4 Pro (14-CPU 20-GPU) offers a 14-core CPU, an Apple M4 Pro (20 Core) GPU, and 36 MB of L2 cache.

In single-core performance, both processors show comparable strength. However, in multi-core applications, the**Apple M4 Pro (14-CPU 20-GPU)** significantly outperforms the **Apple M4** (performance difference well over 10 percent) due to its higher core count.
In gaming, the Apple M4 Pro (14-CPU 20-GPU) is clearly superior.

Its Apple M4 Pro (20 Core) graphics unit has twice as many cores. The higher memory bandwidth of 273 GB/s on the M4 Pro compared to 120 GB/s on the M4 significantly improves gaming performance. The Apple M-series is known for high energy efficiency. The Apple M4 delivers strong performance with low power consumption.

The**Apple M4 Pro (14-CPU 20-GPU)** consumes more energy under load but remains very efficient for its performance class.
The **Apple M4** offers very good value for money for the average user. The more expensive **Apple M4 Pro (14-CPU 20-GPU)** justifies its price with significantly higher multi-core and graphics performance.

passages.heading: Apple M4 / Apple M4 Pro (14-CPU 20-GPU)
passages.text:
Overall the Apple M4 Pro (14-CPU 20-GPU) is faster: 4% ahead in single-core performance and 87% in multi-core workloads compared with the Apple M4.

The most important differences at a glance:

|  | Apple M4 | Apple M4 Pro (14-CPU 20-GPU) |
|---|---|---|
| Cores / Threads | 9 / 9 | 14 / 14 |
| Turbo Frequency | 4.46 GHz | 4.51 GHz |
| TDP | 20 W | 50 W |
| Integrated graphics (iGPU) | Apple M4 (10 Core) | Apple M4 Pro (20 Core) |
| Release date | Q2/2024 | Q4/2024 |
